'''Andrei N. Lupaș''' (born September 6, 1963) is a German-Romanian biochemist, molecular biologist, and bioinformatician.<ref name=MPG>{{Cite web |title=Lupas, Andrei N. |url=https://www.mpg.de/459944/biology-tuebingen-lupas |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=www.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Lupaș was born in Bucharest, Romania, he began his studies in biology at the [[Technical University of Munich]] in 1982 before continuing his studies in molecular biology at [[Princeton University]], where he received his PhD in 1991 with Jeffry Stock on the mechanism of signal transduction in [[Chemotaxis|bacterial chemotaxis]]. He then worked at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in Martinsried in the [[Wolfgang Baumeister]]'s department until 1997. From 1997 to 2001, he worked at [[SmithKline]] [[Beecham (pharmaceutical company)|Beecham Pharmaceuticals]] in [[Collegeville, Pennsylvania|Collegeville]]. Since 2001, he has been the Director and Scientific Member at the [[Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology]] (now [[Max Planck Institute for Biology]]).<ref name=MPG /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-10 |title=The revolution in protein structure prediction |url=https://europe.naverlabs.com/research/seminars/the-revolution-in-protein-structure-prediction/ |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=Naver Labs Europe |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==
Lupaș' research is largely on bioinformatics in combination with experimental structural biology. His earlier research focused on the prediction of coiled-coil structural elements<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lupas |first1=Andrei |last2=Van Dyke |first2=Marc |last3=Stock |first3=Jeff |date=1991-05-24 |title=Predicting Coiled Coils from Protein Sequences |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.252.5009.1162 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=252 |issue=5009 |pages=1162–1164 |doi=10.1126/science.252.5009.1162 |pmid=2031185 |bibcode=1991Sci...252.1162L |s2cid=2442386 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and of proteins, as well as calculations of structural homologies.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Soding |first1=J. |last2=Biegert |first2=A. |last3=Lupas |first3=A. N. |date=2005-07-01 |title=The HHpred interactive server for protein homology detection and structure prediction |journal=Nucleic Acids Research |language=en |volume=33 |issue=Web Server |pages=W244–W248 |doi=10.1093/nar/gki408 |issn=0305-1048 |pmc=1160169 |pmid=15980461}}</ref> Other areas of focus for his research are the origins of early peptides and their evolution into modern domains and ultimately into proteins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrei Lupas fascination for the complex world of proteins |url=https://www.gesundheitsindustrie-bw.de/en/article/news/andrei-lupas-fascination-for-the-complex-world-of-proteins |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025031338/https://www.gesundheitsindustrie-bw.de/en/article/news/andrei-lupas-fascination-for-the-complex-world-of-proteins |archive-date=2020-10-25 |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=www.gesundheitsindustrie-bw.de |language=en}}</ref>

In addition, his research group was involved in the development of the MPI Bioinformatics Toolkit.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bioinformatics Toolkit |url=https://toolkit.tuebingen.mpg.de/ |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=toolkit.tuebingen.mpg.de}}</ref> His research has been funded by the German Research Foundation, the Volkswagen Foundation, the Wellcome Trust, and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute.

Lupaș was one of the judges at CASP14, where [[AlphaFold]] won.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home - CASP14 |url=https://www.predictioncenter.org/casp14/index.cgi#assessment |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=www.predictioncenter.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Toews |first=Rob |title=AlphaFold Is The Most Important Achievement In AI—Ever |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/robtoews/2021/10/03/alphafold-is-the-most-important-achievement-in-ai-ever/ |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>
